title: Console MVP: surgical scope triage for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: We must surgically reduce the initial Console observability surface so we can ship a stable, low-cost MVP for customers. This ticket captures scope cuts, acceptance criteria, and the operational fallbacks that let us defer higher-cost items while keeping high-value signals for platform teams.

Background: The full PRD called for per-route model-variant cost breakdowns, sampled trace flamegraphs, anomaly detection, and a per-token cost drilldown. Projections show those features push storage and query costs >2x for MVP and risk delaying the public alpha.

Proposal: Ship a compact dashboard + on-demand tracing capture for now. Cut route-level cost decomposition and automated anomaly detection from the MVP. Provide a clear migration path: toggles to re-enable deeper breakdowns when sampling/storage budgets are approved. The goal is to retain core SLO visibility (latency, error rate, request volume) and a lightweight cost overview that surfaces large regressions without per-token plumbing.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard default view includes three tiles: 90th latency (per-route aggregated), request volume, and total cost delta (24h and 7d).
Each dashboard tile loads within 600ms for standard queries (pageload measured in staging with 10k events/min synthetic traffic).
Trace capture: UI presents an on-demand "Capture Trace" button that samples a full trace at 100% for the selected request; automatic sampling disabled for MVP (manual capture only).
Cost surface: MVP shows a single aggregated cost metric per-route (total cost and percent change). No per-model-variant breakdowns or per-token drilldowns in this release.
Fallbacks: If backend trace-store writes are failing or cost query exceeds budget, UI surfaces a compact "degraded mode" that hides heavy cards and displays a short message with next steps.
Rollout plan: Feature gated under console-observability-mvp flag; staged rollout to 10% of orgs in week 1, 50% in week 2, 100% after monitoring telemetry meets SLOs.
Telemetry: Instrumentation emits usage metrics for each tile and Capture Trace clicks; cost of storage/month estimated and validated against budget before GA.
decisions: Cut: Per-token and per-model-variant cost breakdowns deferred to post-MVP milestone (reason: high storage/query cost).
Cut: Continuous trace sampling and automated anomaly alerting deferred; instead provide manual on-demand captures for troubleshooting.
Keep: Aggregated route-level cost (total + percent change) to preserve immediate cost visibility for customers.
Implementation: Use compact card UI (single row, minimal data points) for MVP to reduce data volume and render complexity.
tradeoffs: Pro: Faster time-to-market and lower infra costs for MVP.
Con: Less granular cost visibility may delay some customers' ability to attribute spend to specific model variants.
Operational: Manual trace capture increases support load initially; mitigated by runbook and observability playbook included in rollout docs.
updates: 2025-01-10: Drafted scope reduction after cost estimate from infra team showed 2.3x storage increase for full PRD. Added initial acceptance criteria.
2025-01-13: Design review — agreed to compact card visual with toggled detail. Figma mock v2 linked. Action: design to provide collapsed state and CTA for deeper insights.

2025-01-15: Engineering raised concern about trace-store write QPS during capture; agreed to gate Capture Trace behind rate limiter and per-org daily cap of 50 captures for alpha. Added to acceptance criteria. Update: added in telemetry plan.
2025-01-18: PM review with Sales — sales requested a one-click export for cost summaries. Decided to add CSV export as low-cost enhancement in week 2 rather than MVP.
2025-01-22: Stakeholder review complete. This ticket moved to In Review; awaiting engineering estimate sign-off and security review (if required).
